name: Lazarus
overview: Lazarus was a male resident of Bethany, known primarily as the brother of Mary and Martha. He is uniquely noted in Scripture for being resurrected by Jesus after four days in the tomb, a miracle recorded in John 11:1 and 11:44. This event highlights his significant role within the Gospel narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Lazarus, appearing in John 11:1, means 'God is a help.' This proper name reflects a recognition of divine assistance, though it was not given by God directly.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Lazarus as the brother of Martha and Mary, establishing a close familial relationship that situates him within a household known to Jesus. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Lazarus' resurrection by Jesus stands as a powerful demonstration of Christ's authority over death, serving as a pivotal sign that strengthened the faith of many witnesses. This miracle not only affirmed Jesus' divine power but also foreshadowed His own resurrection, making Lazarus a key figure in the unfolding of the Gospel message.
